title_vi: Vì sao HTTP/2 nhanh hơn HTTP/1?

claims.claim_vi: HTTP/2 uses binary message framing and multiplexes request/response exchanges as independent streams, so a stalled stream does not prevent progress on others. The same Introduction says HTTP/1.1 added request pipelining, which only partially addressed concurrency and still suffers from application-layer head-of-line blocking, so HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1 clients use multiple connections to make concurrent requests: common practice, not a requirement; pipelining on one connection is permitted (RFC 9112 section 9.3.2, claim below).
claims.verified_by: draft-ietf-httpbis-http2bis.xml (the source of RFC 9113, which obsoletes RFC 7540 and 8740) read from a clone of httpwg/http2-spec checked out at commit 670dbedffb04d2470cc1ebf2ceccdabc6677a823 (committed 2022-05-31); the cited text was re-read at that revision.

claims.claim_vi: This revision of HTTP/2 deprecates the priority signaling scheme of RFC 7540 but retains the frame field descriptions and some mandatory handling so implementations stay interoperable with those that use it; it does not remove it.
claims.verified_by: draft-ietf-httpbis-http2bis.xml (the source of RFC 9113, which obsoletes RFC 7540 and 8740) read from a clone of httpwg/http2-spec checked out at commit 670dbedffb04d2470cc1ebf2ceccdabc6677a823 (committed 2022-05-31); the cited text was re-read at that revision.

claims.claim_vi: TCP head-of-line blocking is not addressed by HTTP/2; HTTP/1.1 pipelining only partially addressed concurrency.
claims.verified_by: draft-ietf-httpbis-http2bis.xml (the source of RFC 9113, which obsoletes RFC 7540 and 8740) read from a clone of httpwg/http2-spec checked out at commit 670dbedffb04d2470cc1ebf2ceccdabc6677a823 (committed 2022-05-31); the cited text was re-read at that revision.

claims.claim_vi: HPACK is the header compression format for HTTP/2; MDN lists binary, multiplexing and header compression as differences from HTTP/1.1, and says packet loss at the TCP layer can block all streams, which QUIC avoids.
claims.verified_by: HPACK draft (draft-ietf-httpbis-header-compression.xml) read from a clone of httpwg/http2-spec checked out at commit 670dbedffb04d2470cc1ebf2ceccdabc6677a823 (committed 2022-05-31); the cited text was re-read at that revision. MDN read from a local clone of mdn/content.

claims.claim_vi: Chrome turned HTTP/2 Server Push off by default in version 106, citing low use, unclear benefit and missing HTTP/3 support, and suggests 103 Early Hints or preload.
claims.verified_by: Search-result excerpt only; the page itself was not opened (host blocked in the authoring environment).

claims.claim_vi: RFC 9218 (June 2022) defines the Extensible Prioritization Scheme that can replace RFC 7540 stream priority.
claims.verified_by: Search-result excerpt only; the page itself was not opened (host blocked in the authoring environment).

claims.claim_vi: HTTP/1.1 cho phép pipelining trên kết nối bền; server có thể xử lý song song các request dùng safe method nhưng phải trả response theo thứ tự. Nhiều kết nối thường dùng để tránh chặn đầu hàng.
claims.verified_by: Văn bản RFC 9112 đã xuất bản (rfc9112.xml) trong kho httpwg/http-core, commit bde37f634681bd5462568b73aa722af9c9a3ef5e (2025-11-14), mục 9.3.2 và 9.4, đọc từ bản clone ngày 2026-10-14: 9.3.2 cho server xử lý song song các yêu cầu pipeline có safe method nhưng phải trả response theo thứ tự; 9.4 nêu nhiều kết nối thường dùng để tránh chặn đầu hàng. Trang rfc-editor.org không truy cập được từ môi trường soạn thảo nên đường dẫn nguồn chưa mở trực tiếp.

design_notes_vi: Ba nhóm: cải tiến, cần cập nhật, giới hạn; thẻ giới hạn nằm cuối với dải đỏ có chữ. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source presents stream prioritization and server push as features that make HTTP/2 fast; the specification deprecates the original priority scheme and Chrome disabled push by default, so the lesson moves both under 'Cần cập nhật'.
Source's closing caveat that HTTP/2 can be slow is kept and made concrete with TCP head-of-line blocking.
